claims.claim: File a written response with the court.
claims.quote: (3) A direction that the defendant file with the court a written pleading in response to the complaint within 30 days after summons is served on the defendant.
claims.note: The required response is a written pleading.

claims.claim: File it with the court clerk.
claims.quote: file with the court a written pleading in response to the complaint
claims.note: The statute identifies the court, not the clerk specifically, as the filing recipient.

claims.quote: within 30 days after summons is served on the defendant.
claims.note: This supports the instruction to file on time; the draft gives no numerical deadline.

claims.claim: A general denial is allowed when the complaint in a limited civil case is unverified.
claims.quote: (d) If the complaint is subject to Article 2 (commencing with Section 90) of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1 or is not verified, a general denial is sufficient but only puts in issue the material allegations of the complaint.
claims.note: This supports the type of denial, not a particular form. The statute’s assigned-claim exception concerns verified complaints.

claims.claim: PLD-050 is the short general-denial form.
claims.note: The form text was not provided.

claims.claim: PLD-050 may be used in any unverified limited civil case.
claims.note: The statute does not establish form eligibility. The citation description mentions a restriction on assigned claims over $1,000, but its terms cannot be checked.

claims.claim: The limited civil amount ceiling is $35,000, inclusive.
claims.quote: (a) The amount in controversy does not exceed thirty-five thousand dollars ($35,000).
claims.note: The ceiling applies to the amount in controversy, excluding attorneys’ fees, interest, and costs.

claims.claim: A claim of $35,000 or less is a limited civil case.
claims.quote: an action or special proceeding shall be treated as a limited civil case only if all of the following conditions are satisfied:
claims.note: Amount is necessary but not sufficient. Subdivisions (b) and (c) also restrict the relief sought.

claims.claim: If you cannot afford the filing fee, you can ask for a fee waiver.
claims.note: No fee-waiver eligibility or request instructions were supplied.

claims.claim: Use form FW-001 to request the waiver.
claims.note: The form designation and use cannot be verified from the supplied texts.

flags.text: “Any” extends a statutory rule about general denials to a particular form without establishing that form’s eligibility conditions for assigned claims.
A reader sued on an assigned claim could rely on the unchecked PLD-050 instruction, risking a defective response and default.
The definition of a limited civil case treats the amount ceiling as sufficient and omits the relief conditions.
Neither named form was supplied, and the provided filing statute does not specify filing with the clerk.
“If you cannot afford the filing fee, ask for a fee waiver on form FW-001” directs a reader to use an unchecked form based on their circumstances.

result.summary: The sources support timely filing with the court and a general denial of an unverified complaint. They do not establish which defendants may use PLD-050 or how to request a fee waiver. The $35,000 ceiling is supported, but it is not the whole limited-civil classification test.
